FILE ACCESS: your declared outputs are readable. Train 9 tin 1 live-test failure: the board reuse probe still sometimes starts a second board. `boardAnswers` in tools/watch-cli.mjs probes the heavy `/api/board` and aborts at 2 s; on the real launchd board that payload can take longer, so the probe intermittently returns null and `swarm watch --all` starts a second board (observed on 55201/55701). The watch server exposes a cheap token-free loopback `/api/health` that returns `{"ok":true,"version":"...","pid":...}` instantly.

Fix:
- In tools/watch-cli.mjs `boardAnswers(url, fetchImpl)`: request `${u.origin}/api/health` (NO token in the URL, no token header), redirect:'manual', timeout 3000 ms (AbortSignal.timeout?.(3000)). Treat the board as live only when the response is ok and the JSON body has `ok === true` and a string `version` (this distinguishes the watch server from an arbitrary 200). Keep returning false on any error/timeout. The human URL returned by readBoardFile/findRunningBoard still keeps its token; only the probe changes.
- Update tests/one-board-owner.test.mjs: stubs now answer `/api/health` with `{ok:true,version:'1.0.0'}`; assert the probe URL is exactly `${origin}/api/health` and carries no token query/header. Replace the old 'a board answering only with a query token is not reused' test with: a health response that is not a watch health (404, HTML, or JSON without ok/version) is not reused and starts one board. Keep the identity/board.json reuse, stale and open tests green.
- Do not change the identity/board-file URL formats or the launchd update path.

Verify: node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/one-board-owner.test.mjs tests/watch-token-urls.test.mjs tests/memory-fixes.test.mjs -> all pass. Use stubs/temp dirs; do not start a real board.
